target.title: fix: stabilize room-event prompt cache mode
target.body:
Related: #102175

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes prompt-cache churn in long-lived channel sessions where OpenClaw was changing cache-visible prompt/request prefixes between turns.

The user-visible symptom was same-session provider traces with stable model/cache key but cached prefixes swinging from warm (`~49k-52k`) to much smaller prefixes (`~2k-10k`, later `~37k-40k` ceilings) as room-event, sender-policy, and Responses prompt-boundary details changed the request prefix.

## What Changed

This PR now covers three cache invalidators found in the same Discord/channel flow:

1. **Room-event delivery mode vs prompt mode**
   - keeps actual non-internal room-event delivery strict `message_tool_only`
   - adds/threads a prompt-facing delivery mode so system prompts, embedded runs, Codex app-server prompts, dynamic-tool construction, memory/flush runners, and queued followups can use a session-stable prompt contract

2. **Ambient room-event tool inventory**
   - prevents owner/non-owner room-event sender flips from changing cache-visible Gateway tool schemas
   - keeps explicit non-owner execution of owner-only tools blocked
   - preserves the owner-only boundary while avoiding prompt/tool-list churn for ambient room events

3. **Responses prompt cache boundary preservation**
   - stops flattening OpenClaw's internal system-prompt cache boundary into one pre-history `instructions`/system message
   - keeps the stable prefix before replayed history and appends the dynamic/current-turn suffix after replayed history
   - applies this to the agent OpenAI Responses transport, shared OpenAI Responses conversion, and ChatGPT/Codex Responses provider path
   - preserves old behavior when no cache boundary is present

## Why This Shape

The cache-stable prefix should contain durable instructions and tool schemas. Current-turn routing notes, authorization notes, and other dynamic prompt suffixes should not be prepended ahead of replayed history, because that makes the provider see a different prefix every turn.

This PR keeps delivery and authorization semantics intact while making the cache-visible request prefix stable for the reporter's long-lived channel sessions.

## Evidence

Original room-event prompt-mode invalidator:
- Same session/model/cache-key family alternated between automatic-reply prompt text and `message_tool_only` prompt text.
- Prompt-cache reuse varied from near-cold prefixes to warm prefixes despite same provider/model family.
- Source path showed non-internal room events forced effective delivery to `message_tool_only`, and prompt construction consumed the effective mode.

Tool-inventory invalidator:
- Same-session traces differed between `tools=47` and `tools=44`.
- Missing cache-visible tools were `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes`.
- Sanitized gateway log: `[agents/tool-policy] tool policy removed 3 tool(s) via gateway sender owner-only tools.deny: cron, gateway, nodes`.
- After the earlier PR head, live same-session GLM-5.2 traces showed stable `47` tools and cached prefixes around `46.9k-52.2k` on warm turns.

Responses boundary invalidator:
- Later live turns still got low cache even with stable tool inventory.
- Backtrace showed the internal prompt cache boundary was flattened into one pre-history `instructions` string / system prompt message before provider transport.
- The new tests pin the corrected shape: stable prefix before input/history, dynamic suffix as the final input item, and no leaked cache-boundary marker.

Private user IDs, channel IDs, hostnames, API keys, and full trace identifiers are intentionally omitted.

## Validation

- `pnpm vitest run src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.test.ts` — passed, 656 tests.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `pnpm build` — passed.
- Local install smoke: rebuilt `7470c22565f`, installed into LaunchAgent, gateway status running with connectivity probe OK.

Earlier validation on this PR also covered queued followups, embedded runners, Codex app-server prompt-facing mode, dynamic-tool construction, effective `message_tool_only` delivery, and owner-only tool execution boundaries.

Disclaimer: This PR was filed and updated autonomously by Codex on behalf of the reporter; private identifiers were stripped from evidence before submission.
